version.changelog: Initial release: Aave v3, SparkLend, Spark Savings, Kamino. APY tracking, 7d/30d yield summary, health factor alerts.

llm.summary: The skill's documentation describes a DeFi monitor and the instructions are plausible, but the package contains no code and the README's claims (no API keys required, run main.py) don't match the fact that no code or install steps are included — plus on-chain RPC usage may implicitly require credentials; review the external GitHub source before use.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (monitor Aave, Spark, Kamino) line up with the runtime instructions (collect balances, APYs, health factors). However the skill bundle contains only SKILL.md and no executable code, requirements.txt, or main.py — the instructions expect a repository root that isn't included. The SKILL.md points to a GitHub repo, but the skill metadata lists source/homepage as unknown; this mismatch means installing the skill as provided will not actually perform the described monitoring without fetching external code.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are developer-style: create a Python venv, pip install -r requirements.txt, edit config/config.json, and run python main.py. They reference reading/writing only config files under the project and using public APIs. One instruction uses /usr/sbin/lsof to detect a local proxy port (reads system process/port info) — benign for proxy detection but it does access local system state. The SKILL.md also shows cron scheduling examples (persistence via host cron), but it does not instruct the agent to read arbitrary system files or exfiltrate data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only), which is lower platform risk because nothing is automatically downloaded or written by the skill. However, the instructions assume external repository files (main.py, requirements.txt, config examples). The GitHub URL in the document is an external dependency; the package will not fetch that automatically, so the user/agent would need to clone the external repo to run code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials and states 'No API keys required — all data from public endpoints.' In practice, on-chain RPC access (SparkLend) and reliable GraphQL/DefiLlama access can require stable public nodes or API keys (rate limits or restricted endpoints). The SKILL.md also instructs setting https_proxy/http_proxy at runtime (uses env vars not declared in metadata). Wallet addresses are required in config (public info); there is no instruction to provide private keys, which is appropriate. The claim of 'no API keys' may be misleading depending on which RPC endpoints you choose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and defaults allow model invocation — normal. The only persistence suggestion is a user/host cron job example (or OpenClaw cron) to collect snapshots — this is user-managed and not forced by the skill. The skill does not attempt to modify other skills or system-wide agent settings in the provided instructions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package is instruction-only: it contains only a README (SKILL.md) and no code (no main.py, no requirements.txt, no config files). Before running anything you should: 1) Visit and inspect the referenced GitHub repository (https://github.com/reed1898/defi-yield-monitor) — review main.py, requirements.txt, and any third-party libraries for malicious or unexpected behavior. 2) Confirm whether the project needs RPC provider keys (Infura/Alchemy) or other API keys in practice; don’t assume 'no API keys required' is always true. 3) Never paste private keys into config; only add public wallet addresses unless you fully audit the code and understand local encryption/credential handling. 4) Check requirements.txt for risky native modules or network clients and audit any code that contacts external endpoints. 5) If you plan automated snapshots (cron), ensure the machine running the cron is secure and that the scheduled command uses a vetted copy of the repository. If you cannot or will not audit the external repo, do not run its code or give it credentials; treat this package as documentation pointing to external code rather than a turnkey skill.
